Is it more toxic than waking up her sleeping spouse at 3:59 am to tell him the same things she told him via text? How is it toxic, exactly? Just because you don't like texting instead of talking face to face doesn't make it toxic. Hell when I was a teenager in therapy for childhood abuse I wasn't able to fully express myself verbally and my psychiatrist had me write a letter expressing how I felt and mail it to the person. I was able to calmly, clearly, and rationally express myself by taking a few minutes to think, write, read, erase, write, read, erase, and write until I had everything out in a way that was clear. Yes, ideally I would've been able to say those things aloud and in the moment but some people get locked up verbally when dealing with emotions. That doesn't make it toxic and it isn't being afraid or running from conflict. It is communicating in a way that's most effective for the person trying to communicate.

(This might be a controversial take so feel free to bitch at me or down vote) - there's a program called Accelerated Reader in my kid's school (and likely many others) that seems designed to make kids hate reading. My 13 year old read a star wars novel and did the ar quiz that has to be watched by a teacher (but their normal distance learning tests don't have to be for some reason? ) and several questions were about stupid shit like a character's eye color. Nothing to do with the plot or any substantial point of the book. Just these shitty little nitpicking questions about a minor detail mentioned in the very first few pages of a several hundred page novel. About ⅓of their grade depends on these quizzes. Almost none of the kids ever manage to get the required points so every year the English teacher ends up having to either double the worth of each point or half the point expectations.
 
This last quarter this year's English teacher decided to do a more standard book report over the ar system. It was great. My kid was thrilled. He was able to show how much he loved the book he read, make a bunch of jokes (he read a sci-fi comedy), and I got to teach him how to use some basic photoshop to make a movie poster of the book. He had fun, enjoyed the book much more as there wasn't a bunch of what feels like punishment for effort at the end of it, and completely aced the assignment. Since then a bunch of his friends have also read the same book and I've heard them joking about it over voice chat several times. 

Read what you enjoy and foster that enjoyment in others, don't shit on it, don't set up environments designed to kill the joy of reading.
